target: README.md (tracked as readme.md) at repo root, branch audit/release-1.0-2026-07 -- every fenced code block, inline API claim, badge, image, link, install/requirements/extras claim, and the What's-new-in-1.0 feature list, executed for real against the editable venv (hypertools 1.0.0.dev0, python 3.12, mpl 3.10.8, MPLBACKEND=Agg)
brainstormed_edge_cases: README code blocks reference undefined placeholder variables (list_of_arrays, array, blob_a/b, list_of_labels) -- verbatim copy-paste raises NameError [tested: B0-*]
animate=True + per-observation hue (recent QC regression area) -- construct AND render frames [tested: B1, A1]
describe(max_dims=14) on data with fewer than 14 columns (rank < max_dims) [tested: B5e]
describe max_dims semantics: inclusive vs exclusive upper bound (off-by-one) [tested: B5 + source]
align='hyper' on datasets with mismatched row counts [untested -- covered by unit F12-align]
retired 0.x args group=/model=/model_params=/align=True -- error message quality [tested: C16]
cluster(ndims=...) claimed 'removed' in README but still in signature -- behavior with and without reduce= [tested: C16 (silently accepted); docstring read]
legacy 0.x geo files load (weights/spiral hosted datasets) [tested: E2]
pip install hypertools installs 0.8.2 today, not the 1.0 the README describes (pre-release timing) [tested: badge-pypi; install itself untestable-infra]
tests badge resolves on default branch (master) even though 1.0 work lives on dev branch [tested: badge-tests-content]
backend='auto' off-Colab must return matplotlib Figure; backend='plotly' must return plotly Figure [tested: C1, C2]
plotly html renders in a real browser without JS errors [tested: playwright screenshots; only favicon 404 in console]
continuous hue + line fmt = multicolored trajectory on BOTH backends [tested: C3, C3b]
hue as full matrix (mixture proportions) [tested: C4]
colorbar=True for discrete string labels -- are user labels preserved on the bar? [tested: C5 -> finding 011]
cyclic default palette (hls) makes continuous colorbar endpoints identical [tested: C3 -> finding 012]
nested-list input [[a,b],[c]] colors by outermost grouping [tested: C7]
MultiIndex DataFrame expansion: leaf traces + mean trace per level [tested: C8, F2]
soft clustering returns per-observation membership proportions summing to 1 [tested: C9]
pipeline reuse on structurally identical B [tested: C12]; structurally different B -> error quality [tested: C12b]
manip ZScore on a LIST: per-dataset or stacked statistics? [tested -> finding 002]
manip Smooth on a LIST: does the kernel run across dataset boundaries (cross-subject leakage)? [tested -> finding 001]
manip Resample on a LIST: n_samples per dataset or total? [tested: per-dataset]
predict: Kalman/GaussianProcess/AutoRegressor/ARIMA base-install claim + Laplace extra + Chronos HF [tested: C14, N2]
impute PPCA/Kalman fill all NaNs and preserve observed entries [tested: C15]
rcParams mutated by plotting? [tested: C17 -- NONE changed]
misuse: empty list, hue length mismatch, unknown reduce name, animate='bogus', negative n_clusters, bogus kwarg, 1-row input [tested: C18]
plot(bare string) -- text path on a single document -> single row -> zeros [tested: E6 + warning text -> finding 013]

load local formats npy/npz/csv/tsv/txt/json/parquet/mat/xlsx [tested: E1]; real legacy .xls without xlrd [untested: cannot create a real .xls without extra packages; pyproject documents a friendly ImportError pointing at pip install xlrd]
kaggle loader verbatim id kaggle/uciml/iris (anonymous download) [tested: N1]
lsl_stream(type='EEG') with no live stream -- friendly timeout error? [tested: E5 -- excellent message]
gensim Word2Vec README pattern: semantic=None requirement + hidden corpus='wiki' training cost [tested: E3, 110s for 6 sentences -> finding 014]
torch autoencoder reduce [tested: E4]
surface dict form: dict-of-lists (README-suggested reading) vs documented list-of-dicts [tested: E8 crash -> finding 007; F1 works]

animate='window' with focused defaulting to tail_duration == full duration -> byte-identical to 'parallel' (documented fallback; verified md5-equal, then window visible with focused < duration) [tested: A5/E7]
animate='spin' with ndims=2 -- clear error expected [tested: A6 -- excellent message]
morph with per-segment rotations list and surface=True composition [tested: A7b, A7c]
chemtrails/precog/bullettime per-dataset bool lists [tested: A8]
2-D animation for every style except spin [tested: A5]
import hypertools.plot.colors as X / attribute path hypertools.plot.colors.mat2colors (README-documented path) [tested -> finding 005]
readme= file case in pyproject ('readme.md') vs on-disk name [tested: git ls-files shows the tracked file IS lowercase readme.md -- consistent, no case bug]
density=True on 2-D (heatmap) and 3-D (scikit-image iso-surface) [tested: C6]
describe/reduce with ndims > n_features: silent clamp [tested -> finding 006]
HDBSCAN provenance: sklearn.cluster vs external hdbscan package [tested: runtime module check]

findings.title: manip Smooth runs the kernel across dataset boundaries -- data leaks between datasets in a list (contradicts README 'per-dataset manipulation')
findings.description: README lines 80-86 introduce hyp.manip as 'applies a per-dataset manipulation' and showcase a Smooth+ZScore chain inside hyp.plot. The Smooth manipulator's transform is decorated @dw.decorate.apply_stacked (hypertools/manip/smooth.py line 95), so when given a LIST of datasets it vertically stacks them and runs the smoothing filter over the concatenated rows: the end of dataset i bleeds into the start of dataset i+1. For scientists smoothing multi-subject/multi-session timeseries (hypertools' flagship use), one subject's data silently contaminates another's near every boundary. Resample, by contrast, IS applied per dataset (hypertools/manip/resample.py line 110 dw.unstack + per-dataset fit), proving the intended per-dataset pattern. The same stacked behavior affects the README-verbatim chain hyp.plot(data, manip=[{'model': 'Smooth', 'kwargs': {'kernel_width': 5}}, 'ZScore'], reduce='PCA').
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
A = np.zeros((30, 3)); B = np.ones((30, 3))
out = hyp.manip([A, B], model={'model': 'Smooth', 'kwargs': {'kernel_width': 5}})
print(np.asarray(out[0])[-1], np.asarray(out[1])[0])  # expect [0 0 0] and [1 1 1]
findings.expected: Per-dataset smoothing: constant datasets are unchanged -- A's last row stays [0,0,0], B's first row stays [1,1,1].

findings.title: manip ZScore on a list uses STACKED statistics, not per-dataset, contradicting README and its own docstring
findings.description: README: 'hyp.manip(data, model='ZScore') applies a per-dataset manipulation'. hyp.manip's docstring opens 'Apply a per-dataset manipulation'. In fact ZScore on a list normalizes with the stacked mean/std: datasets with different offsets keep those offsets (in z units) instead of each becoming zero-mean. Either the behavior or the wording is wrong; if stacked stats are intended (consistent with apply_model's stack->fit-once->unstack design), README and docstring must say so, since per-dataset vs pooled z-scoring changes scientific results. Single-array ZScore is correct (col means ~0, ddof=1).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
A = rng.standard_normal((50, 3)) + 10.0
B = rng.standard_normal((50, 3)) - 10.0
out = hyp.manip([A, B], model='ZScore')
print(np.asarray(out[0]).mean(axis=0), np.asarray(out[1]).mean(axis=0))
findings.expected: Per README/docstring wording: both outputs have column means ~0.

findings.title: Retired 0.x arguments group=/model=/model_params= die with cryptic matplotlib internals instead of a migration message
findings.description: README lines 137-141 document the retired arguments and their replacements ('group (use hue)', 'model/model_params (use reduce)'). align=True gets a bespoke, helpful ValueError, but the other three README-named retired kwargs fall through **kwargs into matplotlib and produce AttributeError: Line2D.set() got an unexpected keyword argument 'group' -- no mention of hue/reduce, leaking backend internals. Every 0.x script used group=; upgrading users get zero guidance.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
x = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((120, 8)), axis=0)
hyp.plot(x, group=['a'] * 120)
findings.expected: A hypertools error naming the removal and replacement, like the align one: "align=True was removed in hypertools 1.0; specify the algorithm instead, e.g. align='hyper'".
findings.actual: AttributeError: Line2D.set() got an unexpected keyword argument 'group' (likewise for model= and model_params=)

findings.title: README says cluster(ndims=...) 'was removed', but hyp.cluster still accepts ndims= (documented) and silently ignores it without reduce=
findings.description: README line 139 lists cluster(ndims=...) among removed arguments. hyp.cluster's signature still has ndims=None and its docstring documents it as current API ('Passed through to the reduce stage (as ndims=) when reduce=' -- hypertools/cluster/cluster.py lines 187-188). A 0.x-style call hyp.cluster(x, ndims=3) with no reduce= raises nothing and reduces nothing: the exact legacy pattern now silently no-ops instead of erroring or warning, while the README tells users it was removed.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
x = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((120, 8)), axis=0)
out = hyp.cluster(x, cluster='KMeans', n_clusters=2, ndims=3)  # no reduce=
print(type(out), len(out))

findings.title: README-documented path hypertools.plot.colors.mat2colors is unreachable: the plot() function shadows the plot subpackage
findings.description: README line 51-52: 'mapped to colors via the new hypertools.plot.colors.mat2colors'. Because hypertools/__init__.py binds the plot FUNCTION as the package attribute 'plot', the attribute chain hypertools.plot.colors fails (AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'colors'), and the natural import form 'import hypertools.plot.colors as c' fails with the cryptic "ImportError: cannot import name 'colors' from 'plot' (unknown location)" (the function's __name__ is 'plot' and it has no file). Only 'from hypertools.plot.colors import mat2colors' works. The README should show the working import form.
findings.repro:
import hypertools
hypertools.plot.colors.mat2colors  # AttributeError
# and in a fresh interpreter:
# import hypertools.plot.colors as pc  # ImportError
findings.expected: The documented path is importable/traversable, or the README shows 'from hypertools.plot.colors import mat2colors'.
findings.actual: AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'colors'; alias import: ImportError: cannot import name 'colors' from 'plot' (unknown location)

findings.title: describe(): max_dims is exclusive (off-by-one vs docstring) and components beyond the data's dimensionality are silently fabricated
findings.description: describe's docstring says max_dims is the 'Maximum number of dimensions to consider', but the loop is range(2, max_dims), so max_dims itself is never evaluated -- the README example hyp.describe(..., max_dims=14) plots x only up to 13 (the internal helper even says 'from 2 up to max_dims - 1'). Worse, hyp.reduce silently clamps ndims to n_features with no warning (reduce of (100,6) data with ndims=10 returns (100,6)), so describe on 6-column data with max_dims=14 happily draws 'correlations' for 7-13 components -- a flat, fabricated segment at r=1.0 that could mislead dimensionality judgments. The shipped images/describe_example.png also ends at 13, consistent with the off-by-one.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
small = [np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((100, 6)), axis=0)]
res = hyp.describe(small, reduce='PCA', max_dims=14, show=False)
print(len(res['average']))  # 12 entries = components 2..13; 7..13 are all ~1.0 on 6-D data
findings.expected: x-axis reaches 14 when max_dims=14 (or docstring says exclusive); component counts above min(n_rows, n_cols) are omitted or warned about, not silently plotted.
findings.actual: figure x-axis ends at 13 (B5 evidence); with 6-column data the curve continues flat at correlation=1.0 through 13 'components' with no warning (B5e evidence); hyp.reduce(x6, ndims=10) -> shape (100, 6), no warning

findings.title: surface= dict with per-dataset list values crashes deep in matplotlib despite the fail-fast validation, and README wording invites exactly that form
findings.description: README line 56-59: surface has 'a dict form for per-dataset alpha/color/lighting/smoothing control'. The actual per-dataset form is a LIST of dicts (surface=[{...}, {...}], docstring 'bool, dict, or list of bool/dict'; works -- F1 evidence). A user following the README's phrase and writing surface={'alpha': [0.2, 0.8], 'color': [c1, c2]} passes the documented fail-fast key validation (plot.py GH #109) but crashes later in matplotlib with 'ValueError: RGBA sequence should have length 3 or 4' -- no hint that values must be scalars or that per-dataset control needs a list of dicts.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(9)
a = rng.standard_normal((100, 3)); b = rng.standard_normal((100, 3)) + [4, 0, 0]
hyp.plot([a, b], '.', surface={'alpha': [0.2, 0.8], 'color': ['#AA3377', '#228833']})
findings.expected: Fail-fast hypertools message, e.g. "surface dict values must be scalars; for per-dataset control pass a list of dicts: surface=[{'alpha': 0.2}, {'alpha': 0.8}]".
findings.actual: ValueError: RGBA sequence should have length 3 or 4 (raised from matplotlib/colors.py via _resolve_surface_color)

findings.title: Discrete colorbar drops the user's category labels, showing 1/2/3 instead of 'A'/'B'/'C'
findings.description: README: colorbar=True draws 'a segmented, labeled bar for discrete groups'. With hue=['A','B','C',...] the segmented bar is labeled with numeric indices 1, 2, 3 rather than the user's category names, losing the mapping the legend exists to provide (C5 evidence). Scientists must guess which index corresponds to which label (they are ordered, but that is undocumented).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
x = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(5).standard_normal((150, 5)), axis=0)
hyp.plot(x, 'o', hue=['A']*50 + ['B']*50 + ['C']*50, colorbar=True)

findings.title: Default cyclic 'hls' palette makes a continuous-hue colorbar's endpoints the same color
findings.description: With the default palette ('hls', cyclic), continuous hue values map min and max to nearly identical red -- the colorbar for hue=np.arange(n) shows red at both 0 and the maximum (C3 evidence), so the extremes of a continuous variable are visually indistinguishable. A perceptually ordered default (e.g. viridis) for numeric hue -- or a README note to pass palette= -- would avoid misreadings.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
x = np.cumsum(np.random.default_rng(2).standard_normal((200, 8)), axis=0)
hyp.plot(x, '-', hue=np.arange(200), colorbar=True)
findings.expected: Distinct colors at the two ends of a continuous colorbar (non-cyclic default for numeric hue).
findings.actual: hls colorbar: red at value 0 and red again at value ~175 (C3_multicolor_line_continuous_hue.png)

findings.title: Single-row input silently plots zeros, with a garbled warning message
findings.description: hyp.plot(np.ones((1, 5))) (or any single-document text input, e.g. hyp.plot('one sentence')) does not error: reduce returns zeros and the figure shows a point at the origin regardless of the data. The warning text is ungrammatical and truncated-sounding: 'Cannot reduce the dimensionality of a single row of data. Return zeros length of ndims' (hypertools/reduce/reduce.py line 277). Message should read e.g. 'returning a length-ndims row of zeros', and arguably plotting fabricated zeros deserves a louder caveat.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, warnings, hypertools as hyp
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    hyp.plot(np.ones((1, 5)), show=False)
    print([str(x.message) for x in w])
findings.expected: Clear grammar, e.g. 'Cannot reduce a single row of data; returning zeros (length ndims).'
findings.actual: UserWarning: Cannot reduce the dimensionality of a single row of data. Return zeros length of ndims

findings.title: README's Word2Vec recipe hides a large default-corpus training cost (110 s for six sentences)
findings.description: README lines 92-98 recommend hyp.plot(texts, vectorizer='Word2Vec', semantic=None, reduce='PCA'). It works (E3 evidence) but with the undocumented default corpus='wiki' the call took 110.1 s wall time for SIX short sentences on an M-series Mac (gensim training against the wiki corpus), with no progress indication. The README bullet already warns about semantic=None; it should also mention the corpus= default and its cost (or how to train on the user's own documents).
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp
texts = ['six', 'short', 'sentences', 'about', 'foxes', 'markets']  # see claims_ext.py E3 for the real ones
hyp.plot(texts, vectorizer='Word2Vec', semantic=None, reduce='PCA')
findings.expected: Seconds-scale runtime for a toy corpus, or README/docstring guidance about the corpus='wiki' default cost.
